sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface detection by anti-HA antibody staining confirmed in transfected cells (S2R+ and other cell lines); tagged Robo3 and Robo3ΔIg1 showed similar expression levels and surface presence. Slit-conditioned media treatment was applied to HA-tagged Robo3 transfectants (L14), but explicit quantitative functional outcome for the tag itself is NOT MEASURED in the cited clips.
sites.rationale: All fourteen ledger clips describe N-terminal HA tags (3× or 4×) placed immediately after the signal-peptide cleavage site of Drosophila or mouse Robo3 orthologs in full-length, membrane-anchored constructs; surface display is confirmed by anti-HA staining in multiple independent studies. Human ROBO3 has exactly one extracellular terminus (the mature N-terminus at G21, after signal peptide 1–20), so the tag junction is unambiguously insert_after_residue=20, with residue_before=A (position 20) and residue_after=G (position 21), both read directly from the numbered sequence. The position is topology-derived rather than validated because no ledger clip names human residue 20 or 21 explicitly; the closest named ortholog residues are DmRobo3 H21 (L1/L2/L4) and MmRobo3.1 P64 (L3). The tag site is 871 residues from the TM boundary, satisfying all distance constraints. Mouse Robo3.1 (NP_001158239.1) and Robo3.2 (EDL25431.1) full-length constructs carrying an N-terminal HA tag were expressed in Drosophila S2R+ cells and detected at the cell surface; the mature protein begins at P64 (Robo3.1) or P42 (Robo3.2) immediately after the HA tag. Multiple additional clips (L1, L2, L4–L14) confirm the same N-terminal HA-tag architecture on Drosophila Robo3 and mouse Robo3 orthologs, all full-length and membrane-anchored. Human ROBO3 has a single-pass type-I topology with signal peptide 1–20 and a large extracellular domain beginning at G21; the N-terminus is the only extracellular terminus, so the tag position is derived from the topology landmarks.

sources.claim: Mouse robo constructs include the following amino acid residues after the N-terminal HA tag, relative to the indicated Genbank reference sequences: mRobo1 ( XP_006523028.1 , P29–S1615); mRobo2 ( NP_780758.3 , P31–E1508); mRobo3.1 ( NP_001158239.1 , P64–R1402); mRobo3.2 ( EDL25431.1 , P42–K1345).

literature_notes: All fourteen ledger clips converge on a single architectural motif: an N-terminal HA tag (3× or 4×) placed after the signal-peptide cleavage site of full-length, membrane-anchored Robo3 (Drosophila or mouse orthologs). No clip describes an internal loop insertion, a C-terminal extracellular tag, or any tag on the human ROBO3 protein specifically. The Drosophila Robo3ΔIg1 construct (L1/L2) begins at DmRobo3 L119 after the HA tag, but this reflects deletion of Ig1, not an insertion into an internal loop — it does not qualify as evidence for an internal site. The cytodomain-deletion construct (L4, H21–S900) similarly reflects a C-terminal truncation, not an internal tag. No ledger clip supports any internal extracellular loop insertion for ROBO3 or a close ortholog. The single site reported is the N-terminal prepend after signal-peptide cleavage, which is the only extracellular terminus and is robustly supported across multiple independent publications.
